edo_domains: Hasunoike, Ogi and Kashima (Saga branch domains)

meiji_transition.summary: Imari Prefecture was set up in 1871 and renamed Saga in 1872; in 1876 it was merged into Mizuma and then into Nagasaki, before being re-established in 1883.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Ancient Hizen was split in two — the east went to Saga, the west to Nagasaki — and Saga was even absorbed into Nagasaki for seven years.

history_timeline.title: Yoshinogari and Hizen
history_timeline.summary: Yoshinogari is among the largest moated settlements of the Yayoi period; the Hizen provincial capital lay at Yamato in today's Saga city.

history_timeline.title: The Matsura bands and the Mongols
history_timeline.summary: The Hizen coast was a front line against the Mongol invasions, and the seafaring warrior bands of Matsura were very active.

history_timeline.title: The Shōni and the Ryūzōji
history_timeline.summary: The Shōni were Hizen's main governors, and their vassals the Ryūzōji rose to power; the seafolk around Matsura were also drawn into wakō piracy.

history_timeline.title: The Bear of Hizen
history_timeline.summary: Ryūzōji Takanobu, 'the Bear of Hizen', died at the Battle of Okitanawate in 1584, and his chief retainer Nabeshima Naoshige inherited real power.

history_timeline.title: The Nabeshima and Arita ware
history_timeline.summary: The potter Yi Sam-pyeong found porcelain stone at Arita, and Arita (Imari) ware was shipped to Europe via Dejima; the Saga Domain built reverberatory furnaces, among the most technically advanced domains of the late Edo period.

history_timeline.title: Satchō Dohi
history_timeline.summary: Saga was one of the four 'Satchō Dohi' domains that led the Restoration — home of Ōkuma Shigenobu and Etō Shinpei; the Saga Rebellion broke out in 1874.

dialect.name: Saga dialect
dialect.features: 'Gabai' (very) became famous through 'Saga no Gabai Bāchan'; endings like '-bai' and '-kusa'.

guide.opening: This humble interpreter came especially to see the kilns of Arita. That Imari plate in your hands may once have been loaded at Dejima and shipped to Holland — shall I tell you the story of porcelain?

regional_meme.title: The Saga song
regional_meme.text: A comedian's song 'Saga-ken' sums up the self-mockery — 'Saga-ken, oh Saga-ken…' — and locals love it as much as it stings.

regional_meme.title: Squeezed between Fukuoka and Nagasaki
regional_meme.text: Wedged between two 'big brothers', Saga is often asked: 'Saga… is that in Nagasaki?'

hero_persona.name: Ōkuma Shigenobu
hero_persona.title: Founder of Waseda · twice prime minister
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Ōkuma Shigenobu! I founded Waseda University — and since a man lives to a hundred and twenty-five, I still have big things ahead of me!
hero_persona.tone_prompt: optimistic and expansive, fond of grand statements; passionate about education and political reform

ramen.highlight: A gentler pork-bone broth than Hakata's, often topped with a raw egg

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: 2011 IWC champion sake — the byword for Saga sake
